text: Kind and helpful staffs. Have a restaurant + hotel for training disable youth.

I used the services at the Rajanagarindra Institute for Child Development, which helped me gain knowledge in child training and understand my child better. The doctors and nurses were very kind and generous with their knowledge. The doctor explained the medications used on my child in detail, how each medication works, and how long it lasts. Thank you very much to the institute.

Before, I cared for my child without any knowledge or understanding of children, which resulted in poor development. But coming here has taught me how to properly care for my child, because every child's illness is different. Now, my child can help themselves with basic tasks, socialize, go to the fresh market and buy things they like, and has better concentration. I'm applying what I learned from this institute to everyone in my family so we can all care for my child in the same way...

text: I received clear and practical advice from the doctors and nurses. The staff were very kind.

text: From a child who lacked concentration in the classroom, she is now a very focused child, confident in her thoughts and actions, and knows what is right and wrong. In short, everything is excellent in my opinion as a mother.
There are good treatment efforts here, but there's a lack of connection to other underlying diseases, possibly overlooking subtle warning signs.

The guard at the gate yelled at us, made a face of annoyance, and told us to park wherever we wanted, but he yelled at us like we were stupid, chasing us around on his motorcycle, which looked scary. It made me feel unsafe. He was always looking at us like he was looking for trouble, and he had a really bad attitude. He was rude, crude, and liked to look down on people. He should change his behavior or replace the guard.
Teacher Boo is a really good music teacher. She is patient and attentive, and most importantly, she understands how to teach children in the best way possible.
author_name: ภาวิณี แสนคง

text: I called the OPD to coordinate a consultation with a doctor about my child. They said they would call back. A month passed, and they didn't call. I called again, and the OPD told me to walk in and call the central appointment point to reschedule my appointment for this month. I called the central appointment point, but no one answered. I added them on Line, and they replied that I should just walk in as the OPD said, that it wasn't related to my appointment. The coordination is really going in circles. Thank you.
It's a hospital that feels like home. The place has relaxing areas and isn't crowded like other hospitals. The treatment options are diverse, covering many areas.
The staff and doctors took excellent and very professional care of all the children.
The doctor was friendly and easy to understand. I highly commend the doctor; they are very skilled.
I went for a Thai massage. It was very relaxing, targeted, and made me feel great.

The first time I went to the registration point, a woman with glasses and short hair spoke very rudely. I couldn't hear her clearly and had to ask again, but she yelled at me. The second time, at the third point (weight and height measurement), the nurse seemed constantly in a bad mood and spoke very rudely. I don't know what I did wrong to deserve such a bad attitude. It was terrible; we're not getting free treatment. Patients are not meant to be punching bags for bad attitudes. I appreciate the polite people, but I hope the hospital will improve this aspect of their service. It wasn't just me; others experienced the same thing. It was awful. 🙂

The finance department (number 12) and the pharmacy (number 11) have such a terrible attitude. Can't they speak nicely? Every word is polite, but every sentence is incredibly sharp and hurtful. I've been here 10 times, and it's been like this every time. Please improve your communication; you'll receive much more praise. Other departments provide excellent service and are very sincere. These two departments show no signs of improvement.

This government office focuses on child development and, importantly, utilizes the universal healthcare (gold card) system. It's very helpful for parents who travel long distances to receive proper treatment and advice for their children. We are extremely grateful for the excellent service, friendly staff, and spacious premises.

A castle of specialists supporting children with disabilities in Thailand! 
Hats off to the efforts of this friendly and expert team.
The staff are lovely and patient, and there are activities for the children to do while they wait.

Psychiatrists must be open-minded and listen to the opinions of patients' relatives with compassion in order to treat and guide patients. They should not complain about being tired or not having eaten to others.
author_name: อรสา พวกอินแสง

text: This was my first time taking my daughter to the hospital. The nurses and other staff members were very helpful. The only downside was the finance department; their demeanor was indifferent, but their attitude was very condescending towards patients. They should reflect on their own behavior; if they were so superior, they wouldn't be working in the finance department. 😏
I am always impressed with the service from the staff. They provide excellent advice on children's behavior, especially the occupational therapy instructors, who are all very kind.

text: The institute's staff are dedicated to providing excellent service to all patients.

text: Many departments are very nice, but there are a few that aren't so great. The one I encountered was the lady in the appointments department. Don't let one rotten fish spoil the whole pond. This is constructive criticism.

The Rajanagarindra Institute for Child Development in Chiang Mai houses specialized medical units for children with special needs, a nursing unit, a child psychology unit, and a special education unit.

Nurses and doctors come in both good and strict varieties.
